key_concepts: Flame color identifies metallic elements and energy released by excited electrons
Light is a wave with wavelength and amplitude; shorter wavelength means higher energy
Bohr model: electrons occupy fixed energy levels and absorb or emit energy when moving bet
Main energy levels contain sublevels (s, p, d, f) with increasing numbers of orbitals
Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle: exact electron location and velocity cannot both be know
Electron cloud is the probable region around the nucleus where electrons are found
Schrodinger's quantum mechanical model describes electron energies and probable locations
Principal quantum number indicates main energy level; angular momentum quantum number desc
Electron configuration is the orderly distribution of electrons among orbitals
Aufbau principle: electrons fill lowest energy orbitals first
Pauli exclusion principle: no two electrons have identical four quantum numbers
Stable atoms tend to have eight valence electrons
